original_question: For a generic foliation in Ad, the space of foliations on an affine chart C2 ⊂ P2 given by polynomial vector fields Z = P(z,w)∂/∂z + Q(z,w)∂/∂w with max(deg P, deg Q) = d, or for a generic foliation in Bd, the space of degree-d holomorphic foliations on P2, are generic leaves biholomorphic to the unit disc?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4.1 (Anosov): the Anosov problem on the topology of leaves for foliations in A_d and B_d on P^2.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper's actual target. It correctly identifies the two parameter spaces A_d and B_d, gives the affine-chart model Z = P(z,w)∂/∂z + Q(z,w)∂/∂w with max(deg P, deg Q) = d for A_d, and asks the right complex-analytic question: whether generic leaves are biholomorphic to the unit disc.
missing_details: The exact target is Problem 4.1 (Anosov) in Section 4, not a broader discussion item.
B_d is phrased in the paper as the space of holomorphic foliations of geometric degree d on P^2; in the introduction, B_d is introduced for d ≥ 2.
A_d is defined using an affine coordinate chart C^2 ⊂ P^2; this ambient chart should be stated explicitly.
The paper explicitly defines 'generic leaves' to mean all leaves except countably many; your draft leaves that implicit.
The paper does not specify a stronger formal meaning of 'generic foliation' in Problem 4.1 (for example, Zariski-open, residual, or Baire-generic), so a refined version should not impose one.
Nearby context notes that the A_d notion of degree is not invariant under automorphisms of P^2.

Nearby context also records that generically in B_d the foliations have no compact leaf, while generically in A_d the line at infinity is invariant; this is contextual motivation, not part of the question itself.
No nilpotency condition, extra homogeneity condition for A_d, or 'for all sufficiently large m' quantifier appears in or near Problem 4.1; adding any of these would move away from the paper.
refined_question: Let A_d be the space of foliations on an affine coordinate chart C^2 ⊂ P^2 defined by a polynomial vector field Z = P(z,w)∂/∂z + Q(z,w)∂/∂w with max(deg P, deg Q) = d, and let B_d be the space of holomorphic foliations of geometric degree d on P^2 (with d ≥ 2 in the paper's notation). Is it true that, for a generic foliation F in A_d (respectively in B_d), all but countably many leaves of F are biholomorphic to the unit disc?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, for a generic foliation F in A_d (respectively in B_d), are the generic leaves of F—meaning every leaf except countably many—biholomorphic to the unit disc?
justification: The draft is plainly aiming at the paper's Anosov problem because it reproduces the same two parameter spaces and the same unit-disc uniformization question. The only substantive repairs needed to make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful are to restore the paper's own definitions and caveats: B_d is the space of holomorphic foliations of geometric degree d on P^2, A_d is defined on an affine chart C^2 ⊂ P^2 by polynomial vector fields Z = P(z,w)∂/∂z + Q(z,w)∂/∂w with max(deg P, deg Q) = d, and 'generic leaves' means all but countably many leaves. I do not impose any sharper notion of 'generic foliation' because Problem 4.1 itself does not.
